records.text:
Skin biopsy findings:  
- Focal lymphohistiocytic infiltrates beneath a thinned epidermis  
- Circumscribed by elongated rete ridges  
- Vacuoles in the dermoepidermal junction  
- Melanin incontinence  
Images:  
Figure 1. Clinical Presentation Before and After Treatment With Topical Steroids  
Description: A) Numerous 1- to 2-millimeter skin-colored shiny papules on the upper back. B) Comparison of treated right forearm versus untreated left forearm.  
Figure 2. Histological Examination  
Description: Skin biopsy specimen from upper limbs showing discrete foci of lymphocytes and histiocytes immediately beneath the epidermis, surrounded by elongated rete ridges (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification ×10).

bindings.label: The patient developed multiple 1- to 2-mm shiny papules on the upper limbs and body

The patient was diagnosed with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma the previous year and received 2 courses of radiotherapy to the head and leg and 4 cycles of carboplatin, pemetrexed, and bevacizumab followed by nivolumab (3 mg/kg) every 2 weeks
After 8 cycles of nivolumab over 5 months, the papules appeared on the upper limbs, then spread to the rest of the body over the next 3 months, and the patient subsequently developed pruritus
Physical examination showed multiple 1- to 2-mm shiny papules scattered on the upper limbs and body, with lesions on the untreated arm coalescing into plaques
Immune-related cutaneous adverse reaction from nivolumab
Skin biopsy shows focal lymphohistiocytic infiltrates with vacuolar interface changes and melanin incontinence
Skin biopsy shows no atypical epithelioid cell nests or intracytoplasmic mucin
Immune-related lichenoid dermatitis induced by nivolumab
